paraphrase: All things of saṃsāra and nirvāṇa have one ground, two paths and two results — the magical display of awareness and of ignorance. By Samantabhadra's aspiration may all beings recognize the ground and attain perfect buddhahood in the palace of the dharmadhātu.
speaker: Samantabhadra
notes: Reference from the unit author's knowledge (not read in a local text in this phase).

paraphrase: Samantabhadra's account of his own liberation: the ground is uncompounded, self-arisen, inexpressible, beyond saṃsāra and nirvāṇa; recognizing it, one is buddha; not recognizing it, beings wander. He, Samantabhadra, recognized that ground-appearances are his own display and so, without having done a single virtue, was liberated; for beings who did not recognize, ignorance arose as a blank unawareness and a conceptual ignorance, and from them saṃsāra.
speaker: Samantabhadra
notes: Reference from the unit author's knowledge (not read in a local text in this phase).

paraphrase: The aspiration then takes up each afflictive state — desire, anger, pride, jealousy and dullness — describing the realm into which it leads, and prays that, by relaxing into the natural state without grasping or rejecting, each be recognized and liberated as its wisdom.
speaker: Samantabhadra
notes: Reference from the unit author's knowledge (not read in a local text in this phase).
